content: Do we have a deprecation policy for a lemma that is currently public, but is going to become private? #xy: I want to PR steps of the proof of the Riemann mapping theorem separately to make the PRs easier to review. Once the theorem gets merged, most of the steps should become private, because the theorem is strictly stronger.

Also, we have a similar situation with existing results here and there. I'm talking about the cases when the final theorem is strictly stronger than an aux lemma, not about cases like "this construction may never be used for anything else", though we have plenty of these too.

I don't know if we have one written down, but to the downstream user who uses the module system, a previously public thing becoming private is virtually the same thing as deletion. So in my view, the deprecation policy should apply as usual.
Mark as deprecated at the end of the file, then after the deprecation period, mark as private?

My preference would be to mark things private from the beginning. Then there is no need to deprecate. You can add a comment to the module documentation explaining why. Then, if we decide some of these private lemmas should be public, we just do it.

Of course, if this is material already merged and public, then I agree a deprecation period is in order. However, we currently auto-delete deprecated lemmas after 6 months, so we need to be able to differentiate between the two purposes of deprecation.
Yes - I agree that in this situation these should be private from the beginning.
Would the "no public declaration in the new module" linter fire?
Ah I see it is turned off in that file

@Damiano Testa I suppose it's not needed in this case, but could we make the remove_deprecated_decls machinery convert a declaration from public to private automatically if the deprecation date is set to private:YYYY-MM-DD (or some other syntax)?

It is certainly possible to get the automation to switch from deprecated to private. Of course, there will be the need of testing, but it looks like a good training for more audacious automated modifications as well!
